title: Ops econ triage and rollout playback - Peregrine Labs QBR

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-14 15:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Alicia Tran (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (CTO), Ravi Mehta (Head of ML), Samir Patel (FinOps), Hannah Cole (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Discussed recent cost drift after enabling longer context on our prod endpoints; SRE noted tail-latency spikes coincident with cache misses; recommended bench and tuning quantization profiles; plan to evaluate private pilot for sensitive workloads; agreed on next steps and pricing scenarios.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, um Alicia and I will kick off. Quick aim for this call — reconcile the cost drift you saw last month and map a concrete pilot roll out plan.
00:12 Lena: Yeah thanks Jordan. We had a couple gnarly spikes, Samir flagged our bill was up about 28% for May vs April and most of it tied to long-context generation.
00:22 Samir: Right, we pushed the 8k experiment mid-May and there were a lot of long tail tokens. We expected some increase, but not this magnitude.
00:33 Maya: Just to interject, from the infra side the pattern looks like increased KV cache misses and more small batches which drives token cost up per request. There's also a change in p99 behavior.
00:47 Ravi: I want to understand if it's the model variant — are we using a 13B quantized or a 7B in prod for the expanded context? My notes say mixed.
00:56 Hannah: We rolled 13B q4 to a canary lane last week, then widened. We thought quantization would save tokens, but maybe the kernel selection is suboptimal.
01:06 Jordan: Good, this is exactly the kind of nuance we want to capture. Two threads: benching to isolate model vs kernel vs batching, and cost modelling — dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs.
01:18 Alicia: Also adding governance; Lena you mentioned audit and SSO asks from compliance — we should cover that in the short security section near the end.
01:27 Lena: Yep, SOC 2 plus internal audit needs access to request-level logs and proof of encryption-at-rest.

02:10 Maya: Quick note about the p99 — when cache misses spike you basically lose the KV reuse, which forces more compute. For 8k sequences that can change kernel choices and cause a p99 blowout. I saw one trace with p95 about 420ms but p99 at 1.8s.
02:28 Hannah: That 1.8s matches what we saw around 10:15 UTC on June 9th, when our alerting fired. We captured some traces but we can share better logs.
02:38 Jordan: Perfect, Hannah please attach the 2-hour window trace to the Jira.

03:05 Ravi: On the cost modelling side, can Redwood map out committed capacity pricing vs usage-based for our peak/weekend bursts? We need the sensitivity table.
03:16 Jordan: Absolutely, we'll provide a few tiers — small commit with auto-burst, mid commit, and high commit with deeper discounts. We'll also show per-token delta for 7B vs 13B quantized variants.
03:27 Samir: Can you show the unit economics assuming 20% sustained growth? Finance wants the burn scenarios.
03:34 Jordan: Yep, we'll include a 3-scenario forecast.

04:00 Maya: For the bench plan: I'll run a 1,000 request synthetic workload that mirrors your production prompt distribution, compare 7B q8 vs 13B q4 with and without prefix KV cache warmup, and capture p50/p95/p99, token cost, and GPU-milli-second metrics. That should isolate if it's model or caching.
04:19 Ravi: Sounds good — and can you run that on the same AMI/hardware we use in prod? The hardware affects kernel path.
04:26 Maya: Yes we'll mirror the instance type and CUDA versions; if you have custom AMI tweaks please share.

05:02 Hannah: Quick infra note — our cluster autoscaler made a conservative decision which increased latency during the spike; we can tweak scaling, but don't want to mask root cause.
05:15 Jordan: Good call. Autoscaler config is a separate knob but we will include a runbook note.

06:00 Lena: About pilot — we want to evaluate private deployment for a subset of traffic (sensitive user flows). What's the minimal scope?
06:10 Jordan: Minimal private pilot we recommend: 1 model variant, a single reserved GPU pool (1–2 GPUs), VPC peering and KMS integration. Duration 4 weeks for stability and perf. We'll provide a checklist and success criteria.
06:22 Ravi: What do you need from us to start?
06:25 Jordan: Stakeholders, expected QPS for pilot, and a shortlist of prompts. Also a security contact for the KMS setup.
06:33 Alicia: We'll also want to capture rollback windows and an SLA for the pilot.

07:00 Samir: Pricing — is there a way to cap spend on hosted while we validate? We don't want surprises.
07:09 Jordan: Yes, we can put soft caps and alerts. For hard caps we typically recommend a burst buffer on dedicated or strict quotas on hosted. We'll show both options in the pricing sheet.

08:12 Ravi: Any red flags with the 13B quantized variant? We had a couple hallucinations in the expanded context tests but not many.
08:23 Maya: Hallucinations are more model-quality than infra; our job is to keep tokens cheap and latency tight. We do recommend tying regression alerts to your eval prompt set. Redwood Optimize can warn on quality drift if you want.
08:38 Lena: We'd like Redwood to run a quick quality regression check after quantization changes. Is that possible?
08:44 Maya: Yes, we can run an eval on your prompt set as part of pre-rollout checks. Takes ~24 hours to set up depending on prompt count.

09:05 Hannah: Security checklist — we need request-level logs, SSO with SAML, and KMS integration. Also an audit log retention policy — 12 months.
09:18 Jordan: We support SAML SSO and KMS; audit logs retention can be extended under enterprise add-on. We'll share the SOC 2 and KMS docs.
09:29 Lena: Do you have a data residency option? Some EU traffic must stay in region.
09:36 Jordan: Yes, regional routing and pinned deployments are supported in Redwood Private. We'll add region-specific notes for EU.

10:10 Samir: On the billing side, can you break out cost drivers? We saw context tokens spike, but embeddings and reranking ran up as well.
10:21 Maya: We'll produce a breakdown: base model compute, KV cache miss overhead, embedding calls, and small-batch penalties. That'll help identify cheap wins.
10:30 Ravi: Small-batch penalty — can batching be tuned at your side or is it our app responsibility?
10:36 Maya: Both. We have server-side continuous batching but app-level retries and concurrency settings impact batch composition. We'll propose app config changes and runtime knobs.

11:05 Hannah: For the trace we will provide, what format do you need?
11:10 Maya: Any standard JSON traces or the internal span logs are fine — we'd prefer a 2-hour window in gzipped JSON. Attach to Jira ticket.

12:00 Jordan: Let's do a quick recap before we run out of time. Action items — Maya will run the bench and share results, Jordan to send pricing scenarios, Hannah to attach traces. Any additions?
12:12 Lena: Please include the pilot success criteria: 95% of requests under 700ms p95 and cost per 1k requests under $X (TBD with pricing).
12:22 Jordan: Noted — we'll propose numeric thresholds in the pilot doc.

13:05 Samir: One more finance question — if we commit to a 3-month reserved pool, can we ramp earlier and still keep discounts?
13:12 Jordan: We'll include prorated ramp options; usually commit covers baseline and we provide burst credits during ramp. I'll outline that.

14:01 Alicia: Scheduling — is week of Jun 28 the best for pilot kickoff?
14:07 Lena: That works for us. I'll confirm by EOD Friday.
14:12 Jordan: Great. Any final questions?
14:20 Ravi: Nothing else from ML team. Thanks.
14:25 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the benchmark plan and pricing.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker switches and minor transcription artifacts (proper nouns sometimes mangled), some timestamps approximate.
